recent_corrections.text: Two more WATCH-level flags were wrong, both for the same reason. On 7 September a question-framed analysis piece about hybrid warfare, and on 9 September a television studio conversation about domestic tax policy, were each flagged as Baltic security signals. Neither reported that anything had happened. Cause: headlines phrased as a question are already treated as opinion rather than reporting, but that check only looked for a question mark at the very end of the headline. Both of these asked their question in the middle and then added a few words promising the answer, and went straight through. The rule now covers that shape too. Checked against every alert this project has published: three items are newly caught and all three were noise; no genuine alert is affected. Logged here without a separate notification, since the earlier correction today already went out to subscribers.
recent_corrections.context: WATCH alerts 0907-0911 (7 September) and 0909-1156 (9 September) — single-item alerts, both opinion pieces

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: on 8 September, an arts interview about a documentary film on the 1970s Soviet Union was flagged as a Baltic security signal. Cause: a scoring bug. An ambiguous keyword — one that only counts as a military signal when military vocabulary appears alongside it — was unlocked by words almost 7,000 characters away, in an unrelated part of a very long article. Combined with a passing mention of Lithuania, that was enough to clear the relevance bar. Related words must now sit close together to count. Checked against 1,581 live items across every direct source: no genuine signal was lost.
recent_corrections.context: WATCH alert 0908-1224, 8 September 2026 12:24 UTC — sole item from Novaya Gazeta Europe

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Latvia sending about 20 soldiers to the Strait of Hormuz was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. This one was a genuine deployment, not a keyword-matching error like the wildfire correction below — but it's Latvia's own contribution to an international coalition maritime security mission on the other side of the world, with no connection to Russia or the Baltic region. The scoring gap that let this through (a Baltic country's own unrelated foreign deployments passing as a Baltic security signal) has been fixed. As always, the false positive stays in the historical record rather than being quietly deleted.
recent_corrections.context: Latvia plans to send about 20 soldiers to Strait of Hormuz — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-04

recent_corrections.text: A recent WATCH-level flag was wrong: a story about Lithuania sending firefighters to help France fight wildfires was mistakenly flagged as a Baltic security signal. Cause: a scoring bug — generic words like 'deployed' and 'reinforcements' (meant to catch real troop movements) were also matching ordinary disaster-response language. That bug, and several similar ones found in a full audit of the scoring keywords, has been fixed. The false positive stays in the historical record below rather than being quietly deleted — see our policy on this.
recent_corrections.context: Lithuania sends 32 firefighters to help France fight wildfires — flagged WATCH, 2026-08-01

recent_updates.title: The hand-grading of alerts has been removed
recent_updates.text: Alerts are now read in full by the engine before being sent, so grading them by hand afterwards no longer earned its keep. Mistakes still get published as corrections — that record stays.

recent_updates.title: Alerts are now read before they are sent
recent_updates.text: Matching words is not the same as understanding a story. Items that pass the keyword filters are now read in full and judged on what they are actually about. It can only hold something back, never push something through, and if the reading fails the alert still goes out.

recent_updates.title: One source was returning a list of feeds, not news
recent_updates.text: A major Lithuanian source had been fetching a directory of other feeds instead of articles — every fetch looked healthy and returned nothing usable. Now pointed at the real feed. A second source that never dates its articles is now read by a route that does, so old stories stop arriving as new.

recent_updates.title: Two scans finishing at once no longer lose one of them
recent_updates.text: When two checks finished in the same moment, one could overwrite the other's record — one alert was lost this way and has been restored. Both records are now combined instead of one replacing the other.

recent_updates.title: Headlines that ask a question no longer raise the level
recent_updates.text: A headline shaped as a question, then a short teaser, was being read as a report. It is an opinion piece. Those are still shown, but they no longer raise the alert level on their own.

recent_updates.title: Now watching the official emergency channels themselves
recent_updates.text: This page has always said to use your country's official channels in a real emergency. It now reads one of them directly, so it can see what they are saying. Two of the three publish nothing readable — that limit is written down on the method page.

recent_updates.title: Two mentions in one long article no longer count as one signal
recent_updates.text: Long articles could combine unrelated passages into a false signal. Related words now have to sit near each other to count. Caught a culture piece being read as a military one.

recent_updates.title: Reading the defence ministries and grid operators directly
recent_updates.text: More sources are now read directly from the organisations themselves rather than only through an aggregator.

recent_updates.title: This page will tell you if it ever stops being updated
recent_updates.text: This page now tells you if it stops being updated — worked out in your own browser, because a server that has stopped cannot say so. Never treat the absence of alerts as an all-clear without checking it.

recent_updates.title: Every alert now carries an id you can check it by
recent_updates.text: Each alert now carries an id, so a published verdict can be checked against the alert it graded.

recent_updates.title: New: publishing whether the alerts were actually right
recent_updates.text: New: publishing whether the alerts were actually right, judged one at a time. No percentage is shown until enough have been judged.

recent_updates.title: Fixed: alert maps were arriving stamped “API KEY REQUIRED”
recent_updates.text: Fixed: alert maps could arrive defaced by the map provider. Each map is now checked before sending. Thanks to the subscriber who reported it.

recent_updates.title: Browser alerts are retried, and failed delivery no longer goes unnoticed
recent_updates.text: Browser alerts are retried, and failed delivery is no longer missed.

recent_updates.title: WARN now reflects independent confirmation more accurately
recent_updates.text: WARN now reflects independent confirmation more accurately.

recent_updates.text: Fewer false alarms from routine official statements.

recent_updates.text: Fixed: a completed scan could fail to publish and leave this page stale.
